title: Learn ANY Strumming Patterns with this Guitar Exercise
summary: In this JustinGuitar lesson, the instructor explains a practical framework for rhythm guitar in 4/4 time that unlocks the ability to create and recognize strumming patterns. He demonstrates how there are eight potential strums in a bar (down on each beat and up on each “and”), emphasizes keeping the hand moving even when not actively strumming, and introduces a circle-beat method for mapping patterns. The video covers pattern variation, including a common pattern nicknamed “old faithful” (down down up up down) and how to manipulate patterns by shifting which beats are strummed. He provides player-focused practice tips, such as starting with beat one, practicing slowly, then increasing tempo, and eventually playing without chords to automate patterns. The lesson stresses feel and groove as the ultimate goal, and connects pattern work to real songs and playing with others, with additional resources available on the website.
topics: pattern manipulation by shifting strums to beats 2/3/4
old faithful: down down up up down
practice without chords to automate patterns
counting all vs counting only the ands
play-along with track to hear patterns
relaxation and groove over mechanical accuracy
